name: tabor-staff-of-moses
title: The staff of Moses
description: Follow the rod from Eden in the midrash and through the signs in Exodus.
sections: Moses is told to take the rod in his hand and use it for signs. Verse 20 calls it the rod of God.
The midrash traces the rod from Eden through Adam, Enoch, Noah, Shem, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph. After Joseph it enters Pharaoh’s palace, then Jethro’s garden, where Moses takes it.
God tells Moses to take the rod with which he had struck the river and use it at the rock in Horeb. The passage connects the rod across those two episodes.
Aaron casts down his rod. The narrative says Aaron’s rod swallowed the rods of Pharaoh’s magicians.
Aaron’s name is written on Levi’s rod. It buds, blossoms and yields almonds, and is set before the testimony. The passage gives no custody link to the encounter with Pharaoh.
The Jewish Encyclopedia describes a tradition from Midrash Yelamdenu that identifies Moses’s staff with the rod Aaron used before Pharaoh and traces it onward to David.
The midrash supplies a chain within its narrative. The physical object and its modern whereabouts remain open research questions.
